records.title: Polydopamine Functionalized Cu Nanowires for Enhanced CO<sub>2</sub> Electroreduction Towards Methane

funder.name: National Natural Science Foundation of China

metadata.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Electrochemical reduction of CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> provides an ideal approach to convert the greenhouse gas into fuels under mild conditions. Copper electrodes are capable of producing significant amounts of hydrocarbons, but the selectivity to convert CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> into methane (CH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>) remains low. Here, we prepared functionalized Cu nanowire electrodes by coating polymers (polydopamine, PDA) and experimentally verified that the functionalized CuNWs indeed shows 2.3 times higher CH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> selectivity compared with that of CuNWs. The PDA functionalized CuNWs catalyst remains catalytically stable for in excess of 14 hours. We experimentally reveal that the amino groups could be responsible for the capture and delivery of protons for the hydronation of CO* intermediates and phenolic hydroxyl groups for the stabilization of CO* intermediates. The results provide us insights into a new approach to optimize the electrochemical methanation of CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> by polymers that contain abundant functional groups.</jats:p>
title: Polydopamine Functionalized Cu Nanowires for Enhanced CO<sub>2</sub> Electroreduction Towards Methane

records.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

metadata.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Efficient electroreduction of carbon dioxide to multicarbon products in aqueous solution is of great importance and challenging. Unfortunately, the low efficiency of the production of C
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    products limits implementation at scale. Here, we report reduction of carbon dioxide to C
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    products (acetic acid and ethanol) over a 3D dendritic copper-cuprous oxide composite fabricated by in situ reduction of an electrodeposited copper complex. In potassium chloride aqueous electrolyte, the applied potential was as low as −0.4 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode, the overpotential is only 0.53 V (for acetic acid) and 0.48 V (for ethanol) with high C
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    Faradaic efficiency of 80% and a current density of 11.5 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    . The outstanding performance of the electrode for producing the C
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    products results mainly from near zero contacting resistance between the electrocatalysts and copper substrate, abundant exposed active sites in the 3D dendritic structure and suitable copper(I)/copper(0) ratio of the electrocatalysts.
                  </jats:p>
title: Carbon dioxide electroreduction to C2 products over copper-cuprous oxide derived from electrosynthesized copper complex

metadata.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The conversion of CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    into desirable multicarbon products via the electrochemical reduction reaction holds promise to achieve a circular carbon economy. Here, we report a strategy in which we modify the surface of bimetallic silver-copper catalyst with aromatic heterocycles such as thiadiazole and triazole derivatives to increase the conversion of CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    into hydrocarbon molecules. By combining operando Raman and X-ray absorption spectroscopy with electrocatalytic measurements and analysis of the reaction products, we identified that the electron withdrawing nature of functional groups orients the reaction pathway towards the production of C
                    <jats:sub>2+</jats:sub>
                    species (ethanol and ethylene) and enhances the reaction rate on the surface of the catalyst by adjusting the electronic state of surface copper atoms. As a result, we achieve a high Faradaic efficiency for the C
                    <jats:sub>2+</jats:sub>
                    formation of ≈80% and full-cell energy efficiency of 20.3% with a specific current density of 261.4 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    for C
                    <jats:sub>2+</jats:sub>
                    products.
                  </jats:p>
title: Improved electrochemical conversion of CO2 to multicarbon products by using molecular doping
